thread:
Maria Lopez: Legal submitted a DSAR/erasure for an EU customer (RQ-2026-0520). They ask for deletion of personal data and any derived embeddings across our Dedicated eu-west cluster. Need confirmation about KMS-encrypted backups and snapshot replication. @Alice Ng @Devin Ortiz can you take a look?

Alice Ng: Got it. Harry, do we have identity verification attached? Also any ongoing legal holds?

Harry Goldman (Legal): Verified via signed consent form and hashed email. No active litigation hold. I'll attach the scanned verification to the case. Request ID RQ-2026-0520.

Devin Ortiz: Tenant tenant_77 is on dedicated-eu-west-2. They use a customer-managed key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:444555666:key/f1e2d3c4. Nightly snapshots are encrypted with that key and we replicate encrypted snapshots to eu-north-1 for DR (snapshots-eu-west-2 -> backups-eu-north-1). We also keep monthly cold archives governed by 120d lifecycle.

Lina Chen: Vector storage sits in shards named 'dedicated-eu-vs-77-*'. Deletion plan: 1) enumerate vector ids by tenant metadata 2) delete vectors + index entries 3) trigger compaction job. Quick listing example:

`````
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://dedicated-eu.internal.redwood/vectors/query?tenant=tenant_77&ids_only=true"
`````

Note compaction is async and tombstones persist until it's complete. Also check caching layers and eval artifacts.

Samir Patel: Two blockers to note: (1) Because snapshots use the customer KMS key we cannot remove the snapshot objects without either access to decrypt/unwrap or the customer performing key deletion/rotation. (2) Cross-region replicated objects must be deleted in the target region too.

Alice Ng: Proposed erasure workflow:
- Step 0: Legal confirms verification and no hold (Harry) \u2705
- Step 1: Pause any automated ingestion/retention jobs for tenant_77 (Platform, Samir)
- Step 2: Export vector ids and delete live vectors (Eng-ML, Lina)
- Step 3: Purge derived eval sets and caches (Eng-ML, Lina)
- Step 4: Coordinate with customer on KMS key disposition to allow snapshot deletion (Infra, Devin)
- Step 5: Create a short-lived 'erasure-agent' RBAC role (Security) and log assume-role events to immutable audit store
- Step 6: If snapshots cannot be removed due to key control, prepare a documented attestation and partial-deletion report (Legal)
- Step 7: Confirm deletion and close DSAR with the requester (Legal)

Devin Ortiz: I can prepare expedited snapshot purge requests but will need the customer's consent to unwrap/delete or a key rotation request from them. I'll open a secure support thread with their security contact. Note: object lifecycle policies in the cold archive may complicate same-day deletion; we can request a retention-exception to accelerate.

Lina Chen: Will scan eval buckets and caches. Commands I plan to run:

`````
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-evals | grep tenant_77
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-evals/evals/tenant_77/ --recursive
# vector export
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://dedicated-eu.internal.redwood/vectors/query?tenant=tenant_77&include_ids=true" > /tmp/tenant_77_vectors.txt
`````

Lina Chen: Preliminary delete pass removed ~1,102 vectors of estimated 9,300. Streaming deletion log to the case folder.

Alice Ng: RBAC: I'll author a PR to add a time-limited 'erasure-agent' role with granular perms: vectors:delete, snapshots:delete, s3:DeleteObject for the evals path. Important: audit must capture who assumed the role and all deleted IDs. I'll include a runbook for approval flow and TTL enforcement.

Samir Patel: I'll block new ingestion for tenant_77 and file a platform PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4951 (platform: pause-ingest-tenant_77). Also will add an allowlist for oncall operators during the operation window.

Oncall Bot: Task created INC-2026-9010 - "tenant_77 DSAR erasure" assigned to Devin Ortiz, Lina Chen, Alice Ng. Due: 2026-05-02 16:00 UTC.

Devin Ortiz: Support thread with customer linked. Awaiting key action. If customer refuses to delete/rotate their KMS key, Legal advises we must document steps taken and issue an attestation explaining what we could purge and what remains encrypted by customer-managed keys. Harry, please prepare attestation template.

Harry Goldman (Legal): Will draft attestation and include timeline of attempted deletions and communications. We'll also offer the customer a downloadable evidence package for the deletion operations we completed.

Alice Ng: Security request: make assume-role logs write-once and replicate to long-term audit bucket with 7y retention. Filing exception request to Infra for immutable logging retention beyond default.

Samir Patel: Note on KMS: rotating or disabling a customer-managed key without consent is forbidden. We can only request the customer to perform rotation or schedule key deletion. If they provide a key rotation proof, we can proceed to delete snapshots immediately after rotation.

Maria Lopez: Action owners: Devin -> KMS & snapshot purge coordination; Lina -> vector + eval purge and deletion logs; Alice -> RBAC + audit runbook; Samir -> ingestion pause + platform PR; Harry -> attestation text. Keep this thread updated with status and attach proof links. :thumbsup:

Lina Chen: Uploaded deletion logs and a sample CSV of removed vector IDs to the case: https://redwood-internal/cases/RQ-2026-0520/logs (private).

Devin Ortiz: Snapshot purge queued pending customer key action. ETA 3 business hours for next update.

Alice Ng: PR for RBAC and runbook created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/141 (includes assume-role TTL and audit copy steps).

Maria Lopez: Will mark initial intake complete and will reopen if blockers occur. Closing this loop for now. :white_check_mark:
